full_judgment:
17. The basic fact is that Sarat Kumar Kanungoo entered into the contract with the respondent in 1970. He died in 1986 and during all these years she did not bring a suit for specific performance of contract. An attempt was made to show that she was delivered possession of the part of the property in question which, however, does not inspire confidence because of certain litigations over the possession by way of claiming injunction, etc. the suit for specific performance of contract was filed only when the probate proceeding was filed. A simple proposition has been made complicated. The question is whether she is entitled to citation within the meaning of section 283 of the Act. The plain and simple answer is in the negative. So what is the compelling necessity for adding her as a party in a succession proceeding when the question is whether she is entitled to citation if at all. She is entitled to bring the suit for redress of her grievance for breach of contract and she has already filed the suit for specific performance of contract. If she succeeds then the 'suit will be decreed and it could be executed against the executor of the Will. Therefore, she is not deprived of any remedy. Mr. T.H.Khan argued that she could object to the granting of the probate but how will that step assist her in claiming relief in the suit for specific performance of contract is not understood. 

 20. With respect, this test appeals to me because as the learned Judge has noticed that in every case it must be shown that the Caveator but for the d Will, would be entitled to a right of which that will deprive him. In the present case the Will docs not d disentitle the respondent to which she is otherwise entitled. Her case is that of specific performance of contract. If she succeeds the suit will be decreed. 

 21. Section 211 of the Succession Act is the complete answer because it says that the executor or administrator, as the case may be, of a deceased person is his legal representative for all purposes and all the properties of the deceased person vested in him as such. So the respondent is not without any remedy for the execution of the decree. Section 53A creates no real rights. It is estoppel between the proposed transferee and transferor which shall have no operation against 3rd person (See 46 CWN 374 P.C.).
